_note: Seed glossary of curriculum terms. Local teachers should review and extend it; add a language by adding its code to 'languages' and to every term.

photosynthesis.subject: biology
photosynthesis.definition: How green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make their own food (glucose) and give out oxygen.

cell.subject: biology
cell.definition: The smallest living unit. Every living thing is made of one or more cells.

chloroplast.subject: biology
chloroplast.definition: The green part inside a plant cell where photosynthesis happens.

ecosystem.subject: biology
ecosystem.definition: All the living things in an area together with their non-living surroundings, all affecting each other.

force.subject: physics
force.definition: A push or a pull that can change how an object moves or its shape. Measured in newtons (N).

gravity.subject: physics
gravity.definition: The force that pulls objects towards each other. On Earth it pulls everything towards the ground.

energy.subject: physics
energy.definition: The ability to do work or cause change. Measured in joules (J).

speed.subject: physics
speed.definition: How far something travels in each unit of time. speed = distance / time.

velocity.subject: physics
velocity.definition: Speed in a stated direction, for example 20 m/s towards the north.

acceleration.subject: physics
acceleration.definition: How quickly velocity changes. acceleration = change in velocity / time taken.

mass.subject: physics
mass.definition: The amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg). It is the same everywhere.

weight.subject: physics
weight.definition: The pull of gravity on a mass, measured in newtons (N). weight = mass x g.

density.subject: physics
density.definition: How much mass is packed into a space. density = mass / volume.

electric current.subject: physics
electric current.definition: The flow of electric charge through a wire, measured in amperes (A).

voltage.subject: physics
voltage.definition: The electrical push that drives current around a circuit, measured in volts (V).

resistance.subject: physics
resistance.definition: How strongly a material opposes the flow of current, measured in ohms. R = V / I.

circuit.subject: physics
circuit.definition: A complete loop that electric current can flow around.

temperature.subject: physics
temperature.definition: How hot or cold something is, measured in degrees Celsius (°C).

atom.subject: chemistry
atom.definition: The smallest particle of an element that still has the properties of that element.

molecule.subject: chemistry
molecule.definition: Two or more atoms joined together, for example water (H2O).

acid.subject: chemistry
acid.definition: A substance with pH below 7. Weak acids taste sour, like lime juice or vinegar.

alkali.subject: chemistry
alkali.definition: A base that dissolves in water, with pH above 7. Alkalis feel soapy, like soap solution.

fraction.subject: math
fraction.definition: A part of a whole, written as a top number (numerator) over a bottom number (denominator), like 3/4.

percentage.subject: math
percentage.definition: A number out of 100. 25% means 25 out of every 100.

equation.subject: math
equation.definition: A statement that two expressions are equal, for example 2x + 3 = 11.

variable.subject: math
variable.definition: A letter or name that stands for a value that can change, like x in algebra or score in a program.

area.subject: math
area.definition: The amount of flat surface a shape covers, measured in square units like m².

perimeter.subject: math
perimeter.definition: The total distance around the edge of a flat shape.

probability.subject: math
probability.definition: How likely something is to happen, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

algorithm.subject: computing
algorithm.definition: A clear, step-by-step set of instructions that solves a problem, like a recipe.

loop.subject: computing
loop.definition: Code that repeats a set of instructions, a fixed number of times or until a condition is met.

binary.subject: computing
binary.definition: A number system that uses only two digits, 0 and 1. Computers store all data in binary.

data.subject: computing
data.definition: Facts, numbers or information stored or processed by a computer.

network.subject: computing
network.definition: Computers or devices connected together to share data. The internet is a network of networks.

hardware.subject: computing
hardware.definition: The physical parts of a computer or phone that you can touch.

software.subject: computing
software.definition: Programs and apps that tell the hardware what to do.
